current_firmware_to_rtl_functions.test_coverage_gap: The qspi-study testbench executes actual QSPI endpoint/CDC through actual JPEG core, burst memory/SDRAM model, and LCD, but creates QSPI pin transactions itself. No existing test pipes native Sunshine MSV1 output through the production Rust streaming worker/ESP-IDF SPI callsite into those pins. The parser host harness excludes mod.rs/ESP-IDF; the smaller QSPI test has a behavioral core responder, and other JPEG tests use direct core-bus stimulus.

Run scripts/integration_checks.py to execute the real Rust receiver parser against a real JPEG and malformed/recovery corpus. This is the same packet format and JPEG but currently uses Python-produced chunks, not the C++ packetizer output.

Run the qspi-study one-frame test as integrated RTL evidence: its actual QSPI endpoint/CDC, JPEG core, burst memory/SDRAM model and LCD are coupled. Keep its testbench-generated pin source and -Wno-fatal policy explicit; it is not firmware or hardware evidence.

A small next handoff is a host-side adapter that takes actual datagrams emitted by the native Sunshine packetizer, passes them through the production Rust parser/receiver, and maps accepted frame/byte events into the existing qspi-study testbench pin tasks. This adapter is not present yet; do not substitute a fake Rust parser or claim target firmware/ESP-IDF execution.
missing_endpoints: Sunshine capture/encoder and callsite: C++ packetizer accepts already encoded JPEG, is default-off experimental code, and has no sender or protocol negotiation.
Actual firmware worker and ESP32-S3 execution: Rust host harness compiles only protocol.rs, not ESP-IDF streaming::session/forward or device SPI/DMA runtime.

C++ output to Rust input in a single test: tests share an exact golden fixture, but no runner pipes the native packetizer bytes directly into the Rust parser; fixture has u16 records while the stored Rust harness wrapper expects u32 records.

Sunshine/Rust-produced protocol traffic to QSPI pin stimulus: the integrated qspi-study bench currently constructs metadata, reads and payload writes directly in its testbench rather than consuming native packetizer or firmware output.
Target firmware execution: no ESP32-S3/ESP-IDF receiver worker, DMA allocation/scheduling, or actual firmware SPI driver is exercised by the integrated simulation.

Production top equivalence: qspi-study couples the real endpoint/CDC and downstream decoder/display RTL with study-specific guarded JPEG input, tile transpose, burst-memory/SDRAM model; it is not a simulation of the complete moonshine_top source unchanged. No physical FPGA, SDRAM, or LCD evidence exists.
claim_boundary: Existing evidence establishes serializer parity, host-native Rust parser behavior, a separate behavioral-core QSPI component test, direct-bus JPEG tests, and a real integrated QSPI endpoint/CDC→JPEG→memory/SDRAM model→LCD simulation driven by testbench pin transactions. It does not establish Sunshine→actual ESP32 firmware→QSPI pins→display integration, CS88 integration, physical timing, or hardware operation.
